meta.title: Azmin Yusmizan | Electrical engineering, embedded systems and RF
hero.lead: Final-year electrical engineering student at INSA Lyon. I build long-range radio links, bare-metal firmware and the circuits underneath them.
hero.caption: A stylized LoRa frame, the modulation behind my latest project: preamble upchirps, sync downchirps, then data symbols. Channel 1 is the baseband signal, channel 2 its instantaneous frequency.
case.context: Featured project, Num'axes R&D, October 2025 to February 2026
case.title: Tracking hunting dogs where there is no network
case.p1: A hunter following several dogs through dense forest needs to see where each one is, make a collar beep to find it, and keep receiving positions when a ridge cuts the radio link. Commercial products either rely on a cellular subscription or stop at two dogs with no relay.
case.p2: During my R&D internship at Num'axes I designed, built and validated a prototype that does all of this over LoRa, peer to peer: no gateway, no smartphone, no network operator. I wrote the radio protocol and the firmware for both the collars and the handheld remotes.
case.s1d: LoRa peer to peer, 869.4 MHz (EU868), SF7, 125 kHz, CR 4/5, 14 dBm
case.s2d: Up to 9 collars and 3 remotes, no infrastructure
case.s3d: 8 bytes, 41.2 ms on air (was 11 bytes, 51.5 ms: −19.9%)
case.s4d: 4 bytes, 36.1 ms on air (was 7 bytes, 41.2 ms: −12.4%)
case.s5d: G ≈ 0.068 with a full group, about 87% first-try delivery (pure ALOHA model)
case.s7d: C, bare-metal, event-driven; one codebase built for both roles
case.s8d: Collar ≈ 117 h, remote ≈ 27 h on 2000 mAh (prototype, sleep modes not yet enabled)
case.dCollars: GNSS collars, one position every 6 s
case.diagCap: When remote A loses collar 3 behind terrain, it asks the best-placed remote to relay. One helper at a time, every step bounded by a timeout, and each forwarded message carries an ID and a hop limit so nothing is transmitted twice.
case.t1: I started with verbose frames for debugging, then designed compact v2 frames: positions packed as signed 24-bit coordinates (10<sup>−4</sup> degree) with a fix flag, commands tagged with a sequence number. Every command (beep, vibration, mute, volume) is acknowledged end to end; duplicates are recognized and re-acknowledged without being executed twice. Pairing only accepts requests inside a time window.
case.t2: The owner's remote picks a helper from how recently it heard the dog and how close it is by GNSS. Commands go through a request, offer, grant and forward handshake, with the acknowledgement routed back to the owner. Positions are forwarded under a time-limited lease. If the best helper times out, the next candidate is tried.
case.h3: Reading a competitor's radio from its SPI bus
case.t3: To ground our design choices, I measured a competing tracker's channels on a spectrum analyzer, then tapped the SPI bus between its microcontroller and LoRa transceiver with a logic analyzer. Decoding the register writes against the transceiver datasheet revealed its real settings (SF8, 62.5 kHz). That analysis is why we chose SF7 at 125 kHz: shorter airtime, better suited to many nodes.
case.h4: An immobility alarm that ignores breathing
case.t4: GNSS drifts too much under tree cover to tell whether a pointing dog has stopped, so the collar uses an accelerometer instead. The algorithm tracks changes between samples to cancel gravity, smooths them with an IIR filter and applies hysteresis: 5 s of stillness raises the alarm, 400 ms of clear movement clears it.
case.t5: Every event is logged over UART with its radio metrics, and each scenario (pairing, commands, GNSS, relay, alarm) has a reproducible test with pass criteria. A few lines from the test campaign:
case.t6: The remote is the autonomy bottleneck at about 27 h, so the largest gain will come from duty-cycled reception rather than fewer transmissions. After that: a dedicated PCB and enclosure, adaptive GNSS reporting when the dog is still, collision backoff, and a wider field campaign in dense, hilly terrain.
exp.title: Experience
exp.lead: Two internships at Num'axes, a French company that designs and sells electronic devices for dog training, containment and tracking across Europe and Asia.
exp.1role: R&D engineering intern, embedded systems and radio
exp.1b1: Designed and validated an infrastructure-free LoRa tracking prototype for up to 9 GNSS collars and 3 handheld remotes.
exp.1b2: Specified the application protocol: compact frames cutting time-on-air by up to 19.9%, end-to-end acknowledged commands with deduplication, and time-windowed pairing.
exp.1b3: Built a controlled relay mechanism with message IDs, hop limits and sequential fallback to keep tracking dogs when the direct link drops.
exp.1b4: Wrote layered bare-metal C firmware on the Microchip WLR089U0 (BSP, radio HAL, protocol, services, UI), integrating u-blox GNSS and an accelerometer-based immobility alarm.
exp.1b5: Reverse-engineered a competitor's radio link by spectrum analysis and SPI bus sniffing; the findings set our radio parameters.
exp.2b1: Designed a custom PCB for a dog collar system, covering both the analog and digital schematics and the board layout.
exp.2b2: Simulated circuits in LTspice and validated them on protoboard before committing to layout.
exp.2b3: Iterated through testing, component validation and debugging in an R&D team, under real product constraints such as EMC and form factor.
proj.title: Projects
proj.lead: Academic and industrial projects from IUT Paul Sabatier, INSA Lyon and Num'axes, from analog front ends to radio and automation.
proj.loraD: Infrastructure-free tracking over LoRa with GNSS collars, acknowledged commands, a controlled relay and an immobility alarm.
proj.sonoD: A complete sonometer built from the ground up: circuit design, LTspice simulation, prototyping and PCB fabrication, grounded in acoustic measurement principles.
proj.dustD: Dust detection system with a custom circuit and embedded software, with a focus on sensor calibration for environmental monitoring.
proj.sortD: GRAFCET-based control of an industrial line that sorts parts by color and number, with a complete workflow across several control stations.
proj.medD: Machine-learning algorithms for brain image analysis and classification, applying numerical analysis and data processing to diagnostic support.
proj.regD: Co-founded a student startup developing intelligent electrical regulation: business plan, prototype and a mobile app to optimize consumption.
proj.lineD: A complete robot from schematic to PCB, integrating sensors, motors and path-following control.
proj.carD: Autonomous vehicle controlled from a smartphone, with multiple sensors and wireless communication.
proj.pneuD: Pneumatic handling station programmed in TIA Portal, part of a team project linking several automated stations.
proj.scanD: 3D scanning and data acquisition system built on an STM32 microcontroller with distance sensors and servo motors.
proj.ecgD: ECG acquisition chain with analog amplifiers, filters and signal conditioning for biomedical signals.
proj.filtD: Anti-aliasing and smoothing filters, designed and implemented on PCB for signal conditioning.
proj.audioD: Real-time guitar effects written in C, including reverb and distortion.
proj.liqD: RF sensor that tells water from ethanol, designed in Cadence AWR with Smith chart analysis and a custom PCB with precise copper traces.
proj.iotD: Distributed sensor-actuator network on STM32 microcontrollers with wireless links, for environmental monitoring and control.
proj.antD: Reverse-engineered and optimized a patch antenna in Cadence AWR, reaching a −17 dB reflection coefficient at the target frequency.
proj.solarD: Photovoltaic modeling, simulation and experimental characterization to analyze conversion efficiency.

skills.g4d: Real-time DSP in C, IIR filtering, image processing in C++, protocol and state-machine design.
skills.g5d: Siemens TIA Portal, GRAFCET, pneumatic actuation, multi-station industrial control.

about.title: About me
about.p1: I'm Azmin, an electrical engineering student from Malaysia. I have studied in France since 2021, first in Tours, then Toulouse, now Lyon. Working across different schools and technical cultures has made me detail-oriented and adaptable.
about.p2: What I enjoy most is the step from idea to working hardware: measuring before concluding, finding out why something doesn't work, fixing it, and documenting it while it's fresh. Whether it's a radio protocol, a filter board or an antenna, I like solutions that are practical and clean.
about.p3: Away from the bench, reading, cooking, running, drawing, guitar and travel keep me curious and balanced.

pp.title: Privacy policy
pp.summary: In short: this site sets no cookies and uses no analytics, advertising or tracking. The only personal data I receive is what you choose to send me through the contact form or by email, and I use it only to reply to you.
pp.p1: This website is the personal, non-commercial portfolio of Muhammad Azmin Muhamad Yusmizan, a student living in Villeurbanne, France. I am the controller of the personal data described below within the meaning of the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). You can reach me at muhammad-azmin.muhamad-yusmizan@insa-lyon.fr.
pp.h2: What data is processed, and why
pp.p2a: The site is hosted by GitHub Pages (GitHub, Inc., USA). To deliver the pages and protect the service, GitHub's servers process technical data such as your IP address, browser type and the pages requested, and may keep them in server logs. I have no access to these logs. The legal basis is my legitimate interest in running a secure, working website (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR). See the GitHub General Privacy Statement.
pp.p2b: The typefaces are loaded from Bunny Fonts, operated by BunnyWay d.o.o. in Slovenia (EU). Your browser connects to their servers to download the font files. Bunny Fonts states that it does not log or store personal data from these requests. See fonts.bunny.net/about.
pp.p2c: If you use the contact form, your name, email address and message are sent to Formspree, Inc. (USA), which forwards them to my inbox. I use them only to read and answer your message. The legal basis is your consent, given by ticking the box on the form (Article 6(1)(a) GDPR); you can withdraw it at any time by emailing me. Because Formspree processes data in the United States, your message leaves the EU; Formspree describes how it protects this data in its privacy policy. If you prefer, you can simply email me instead.
pp.p2d: If you email me directly, your message is handled by the INSA Lyon email service. I use it only to reply to you.
pp.p2e: If you choose a language other than English, that choice is saved in your browser's local storage under the key lang, so the site remembers it on your next visit. It never leaves your device and is not a tracking tool, so it does not require consent. You can delete it by clearing your browser's site data.
pp.p3: I keep messages for as long as our conversation is useful, and delete them at the latest 12 months after our last exchange, unless we agree to stay in touch professionally. Formspree and GitHub apply their own retention periods, described in their policies.
pp.h4: What this site does not do
pp.l1: No cookies, analytics, advertising or social media trackers.
pp.l2: No selling, renting or sharing of your data with anyone other than the providers named above.
pp.p4: Links to LinkedIn and GitHub take you to their own websites, which have their own privacy policies.
pp.p5: Under the GDPR you have the right to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict or object to its processing, to data portability, and to withdraw your consent at any time. To exercise any of these rights, email me; I will answer within one month. If you think your data has been handled unlawfully, you can lodge a complaint with the French data protection authority, the CNIL (www.cnil.fr), or with the authority in your own EU country.
pp.p6: If the way this site handles data changes, for example if a new service is added, I will update this page and the date at the top.
pp.p7: Publisher: Muhammad Azmin Muhamad Yusmizan, private individual, contact muhammad-azmin.muhamad-yusmizan@insa-lyon.fr. Host: GitHub, Inc., 88 Colin P. Kelly Jr. Street, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA.
